preconditions.expression: T == int(stdin.split()[0]) and T >= 1 and T <= 5
preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 5) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line is an integer N (2 ≤ N ≤ 10^5) representing the number of nodes in the tree.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == N-1 for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]) and all(1 <= int(p) < i+1 for i, line in enumerate(stdin.splitlines()[2::2]) for p in line.split())
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line contains N-1 space-separated integers p_1, ..., p_{N-1} where p_i is the parent of node i+1 (1 ≤ p_i < i+1). This defines a valid tree rooted at node 1.

postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is a single integer representing the maximum possible sum of subtree MEX values (a_1 + ... + a_N) when assigning each integer from 0 to N-1 exactly once to the nodes. The function compute_max_sums(stdin) parses the input and returns a list of these maximum sums for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= max_sum <= N*(N-1)//2 for max_sum in compute_max_sums(stdin))
postconditions.description: The maximum sum for each test case is a non-negative integer bounded by the theoretical maximum possible sum (N*(N-1)//2).
